title: Orion Watches over Paranal
caption: Orion and the Milky Way above the VLT Survey Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The soft glow of the Milky Way pours like a waterfall over the VLT Survey Telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory. Just outside the galaxy's band, a few stars stand out. The bright reddish one is Betelgeuse and the fainter white star to its left is Bellatrix, the two shoulders of Orion the Hunter. Above them, three stars in a straight line form Orion's belt, and nearby is the purple-tinged glow of the Orion Nebula.

Betelgeuse, a red supergiant some 640 light-years off, is thought to be close to exploding as a supernova. The Orion Nebula looks like a fuzzy patch to the naked eye, but binoculars or a telescope show a nebula where huge amounts of star formation are taking place.

At 2635 metres above sea level, the VST enjoys exceptionally clear skies. It is the largest telescope in the world devoted to surveying the sky in visible light, and its work ranges from finding remote Solar System bodies to studying our galaxy's structure.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph at ESO's Paranal Observatory, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A camera exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the Orion Nebula's purple tint and the Milky Way's glow appear stronger than they would to an observer.

explore: The VST also searches for exoplanet transits, the slight dimming when a planet crosses in front of its star, and contributes to studies of how our galaxy has evolved.
alt: The Milky Way above the VLT Survey Telescope, with a bright reddish star, a white star, three stars in a row and a small purple glow nearby.
